questions.question: Free Trade Agreement is a trigger on EVERY player's turn, and the options are phrased from 'that player's' side ('that player may draw a card and their opponent may play a resource'; 'Both players may draw up to 2 cards'). At 3+ players, which player is 'their opponent' and who are 'both players'?
readings: (A) The active player ('that player') selects one opponent of theirs for the chosen option's block; 'their opponent' is that player, and 'both players' = the active player and that selected opponent.

(B) Literal MP 2/MP 3 from the card controller's side: P1 (controller) selects 'your opponent'; 'their opponent' = P1's selected opponent and 'both players' = P1 and that opponent, even if neither is the active player.
(C) Every player other than the active player is 'their opponent'; 'both players' = every player (the two-player data generalised).
questions.recommendation: (A). The option text is written from the active player's side (they choose, 'that player', 'their opponent'), so the selection MP 2/MP 3 call for is theirs; (B) would let the active player's option affect two players neither of whom is them, and (C) contradicts the singular printed 'their opponent' / 'both players'.

questions.question: 'If your opponent plays a card, remove a token from this card.' A trigger condition names 'your opponent', but triggers choose their opponent only when they resolve. Which opponent's play triggers it?
readings: (A) Any opponent's play triggers it; the acting opponent is the block's 'your opponent' (the condition is satisfied by whichever opponent acted, like 'only during your opponent's turn' is satisfied by choosing the active player).
(B) It is lasting text: P1 chooses the opponent when the card enters play (RQ-mp-5) and only that player's plays trigger it; if that player is eliminated P1 chooses again.
questions.recommendation: (A). It matches how conditions are satisfied by the choice (MP 2) and needs no standing choice for a pure trigger. Same answer as MPQ-1st-edition-2.

questions.question: 'If you attack, your opponent picks any number of characters they control. Those characters must block during this battle if they can, and only those characters can block.' With 3+ players only the defending player forms the blocking party. Which player is 'your opponent'?
readings: (A) Literal MP 2/MP 4: P1 selects any opponent when the trigger resolves. If a non-defender is selected, the defender may not block at all (only the selected player's characters may block, and they are not in the battle).
(B) The defending player of this battle is the only legal choice (the trigger is about the battle's blocking side).
questions.recommendation: (A). It is what MP 2 and the trigger rule say literally, and it needs no new rule; (B) is the fix if choosing a non-defender is judged an exploit (a house-rule-sized decision).
